name: Opposite Sharp Two-Arm Systems Have Three Alternating Support Graphs
statement: Suppose both relative wings of an ample two-layer family attain the sharp two-arm holonomy equality. For each arm, pair the direction of its shore edge with its passive direction. Within each wing the two support pairs are disjoint, all four support pairs are distinct, and either three are pairwise disjoint or the colored support graph is an alternating four-cycle, an alternating four-edge path, or two disjoint alternating two-edge paths.
proof: In the equality description, the common lower family is an active core with two pendant three-edge arms. Every arm edge is a bridge and therefore the unique edge of its coordinate class, so the six arm directions are distinct and the two support pairs in one wing are disjoint. Each terminal active--passive square is shattered by its wing but not by the common section: the passive direction labels only one common-section edge, whereas a shattered square requires two. The pair-rich opposite-wing theorem now gives four distinct pairs and exactly the three exceptional incidence forms.
